title: Spaghetti Bolognese
summary: Slow-simmered beef and pancetta ragù enriched with white wine, tomatoes and milk, served with pasta and Parmesan.

stages.title: Soften the soffritto
steps: Heat olive oil in a heavy-based pot over medium-low heat. Add pancetta and cook for 4–5 minutes until its fat renders.
Add onion, carrot and celery and cook gently for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until soft but not browned.

stages.title: Brown the beef
steps: Increase heat to medium, add beef and break it into small pieces with a wooden spoon.
Cook until the meat loses its pink colour and the released liquid has evaporated; allow a little browning for depth.

stages.title: Reduce the wine
steps: Pour in white wine and scrape any browned bits from the base of the pan.
Simmer until the wine has almost completely evaporated so the sauce tastes rounded rather than alcoholic.

stages.title: Slow-simmer the ragù
steps: Stir in passata and 150 ml stock or water. Season lightly and bring to a very gentle simmer.
Partially cover and cook for about 100 minutes, stirring occasionally; add a splash of water whenever the sauce starts sticking or drying out.

stages.title: Finish with milk
steps: Stir in milk and continue simmering gently for 25–30 minutes until the meat is tender and sauce thick.
Taste and adjust salt and pepper. The finished ragù should be meaty and moist, not watery.

stages.title: Cook pasta and serve
steps: Boil pasta in well-salted water until al dente; reserve a cup of pasta water before draining.
Toss pasta with ragù and a splash of pasta water, then serve with grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

tips: Use beef with some fat; extra-lean mince can turn dry during long cooking.
Keep the simmer very gentle: rapid boiling toughens the meat and dries the sauce.
Tagliatelle is the traditional pairing in Bologna.
variations: Replace 100 g beef with 100 g pork mince for a richer ragù.
Use tagliatelle instead of spaghetti for a more traditional presentation.
storage: Cool promptly. Refrigerate ragù up to 3–4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat until steaming hot; cook pasta fresh.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
summary: Tender chicken in a creamy tomato curry fragrant with ginger, garlic, garam masala and warming spices.
ingredients: 650 g boneless chicken thighs, cut into 3 cm pieces
1 tsp salt, plus more to taste
Fresh coriander and cooked basmati rice, to serve

stages.title: Marinate the chicken
steps: Mix yoghurt, lemon juice, half the garlic and ginger, half the garam masala, 1 tsp cumin, paprika and salt.
Coat chicken thoroughly and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes if possible; keep chilled until cooking.

stages.title: Sear the chicken
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide heavy pan over medium-high heat. Lift chicken from marinade, letting excess drip off.
Sear in batches for 2–3 minutes per side until lightly charred; the chicken will finish cooking in the sauce.

stages.title: Build the spiced base
steps: Lower heat to medium and add remaining oil and onion. Cook 6–8 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in remaining garlic, ginger, garam masala, cumin, turmeric and chilli powder; cook 30 seconds until fragrant without burning.

stages.title: Simmer the tomato sauce
steps: Add crushed tomatoes and 100 ml water. Scrape up browned bits and simmer 10–12 minutes until slightly thickened.
For a smooth restaurant-style sauce, carefully blend the sauce before returning it to the pan.

stages.title: Finish the chicken
steps: Stir in cream, add seared chicken and any juices, and simmer gently for 8–12 minutes.
Check the thickest piece reaches 75°C, season to taste, and serve with rice and coriander.

tips: Thigh meat stays juicier than breast during simmering.
Avoid boiling vigorously after adding cream to prevent splitting.
Cook chicken in batches so it sears rather than steams.
variations: Use coconut cream instead of dairy cream for a different flavour (the yoghurt marinade still contains dairy).
Add 150 g baby spinach during the final 2 minutes.
storage: Cool promptly and refrigerate up to 3 days; freeze sauce and chicken up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly.

title: Thai Green Chicken Curry
summary: Chicken and vegetables simmered in fragrant green curry paste, coconut milk, Thai basil and lime.
ingredients: 1 tsp palm sugar or brown sugar

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Slice chicken into even bite-sized pieces and dice aubergine into 2 cm cubes.
Trim green beans and slice capsicum so the vegetables cook at similar speeds.

stages.title: Fry the curry paste
steps: Heat oil and 3 tbsp of the thick coconut cream from the top of the tin in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add green curry paste and stir-fry 2–3 minutes until aromatic; add a splash of coconut milk if it starts catching.

stages.title: Simmer chicken and aubergine
steps: Pour in remaining coconut milk and stock, stirring until smooth. Add lime leaves, chicken and aubergine.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chicken is nearly cooked and aubergine softens.

stages.title: Add vegetables and balance
steps: Add green beans and capsicum; simmer 4–6 minutes until just tender and chicken reaches 75°C.
Season with fish sauce and sugar, adjusting until savoury, lightly sweet and fragrant.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Turn off heat and fold in Thai basil so its aroma stays fresh.
Serve immediately over jasmine rice with lime wedges for squeezing.

tips: Taste the curry paste before adding extra chilli; brands vary greatly in heat.
Keep coconut milk at a gentle simmer to maintain a smooth sauce.
variations: Use firm tofu and vegetable stock; replace fish sauce with soy sauce for a vegetarian version.
Swap aubergine for courgette, adding it later so it stays tender-crisp.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; freeze up to 2 months. Reheat gently until piping hot; store rice separately and chill promptly.

title: Classic Beef Lasagne
summary: Layers of tender beef ragù, silky béchamel and pasta baked beneath a golden, bubbling cheese crust.

stages.title: Cook the ragù base
steps: Heat olive oil in a deep pan. Cook pancetta for 3 minutes, then add onion, carrot and celery and soften for 8 minutes.
Add mince and brown thoroughly, breaking up lumps; stir in tomato paste and cook 1 minute.

stages.title: Simmer the meat sauce
steps: Pour in wine and reduce by half, scraping up any browned bits. Add tomatoes and stock.
Simmer uncovered for 40–45 minutes until thick but spoonable, stirring occasionally; season with salt and pepper.

stages.title: Make the béchamel
steps: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium-low heat; whisk in flour and cook for 1–2 minutes without browning.
Gradually whisk in milk and simmer 5–7 minutes until smooth and thick enough to coat a spoon. Add nutmeg, salt and pepper.

stages.title: Layer the lasagne
steps: Heat oven to 190°C conventional (170°C fan). Spread a thin layer of ragù in a 23 x 33 cm baking dish.
Layer pasta sheets, ragù, béchamel and a little Parmesan; repeat, finishing with béchamel, Parmesan and mozzarella. Check packet instructions for dried sheets.

stages.title: Bake and rest
steps: Cover loosely with foil and bake 25 minutes; remove foil and bake another 15–20 minutes until bubbling and golden.
Rest for 15 minutes before slicing so the layers hold together.

tips: Keep ragù fairly thick to avoid a watery lasagne.
Resting after baking makes serving much neater.
variations: Add 150 g sautéed mushrooms to the ragù.
Replace part of the beef with pork mince for a fuller flavour.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze individual portions up to 3 months. Reheat until steaming hot throughout.

title: Shakshuka
summary: Eggs gently poached in a smoky tomato and pepper sauce with cumin, paprika and fresh herbs.

stages.title: Soften the vegetables
steps: Heat olive oil in a wide lidded frying pan over medium heat. Add onion and capsicum.
Cook 8–10 minutes until the vegetables soften and the onion becomes translucent.

stages.title: Toast the spices
steps: Add garlic, cumin, smoked paprika and chilli flakes.
Stir for 30–60 seconds until fragrant, taking care not to scorch the garlic.

stages.title: Reduce the tomato sauce
steps: Add chopped tomatoes and season with salt and pepper.
Simmer uncovered for 10–12 minutes until the sauce thickens enough to hold shallow wells. Taste and adjust seasoning.

stages.title: Poach the eggs
steps: Make six small wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook over low heat for 5–8 minutes until whites are set and yolks are cooked to your preference.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Scatter with chopped parsley or coriander.
Bring the pan to the table and serve with bread for scooping up the sauce.

tips: Use a wide pan so the eggs cook evenly.
For firmer yolks, leave the lid on for an extra minute or two.
variations: Add crumbled feta just before serving.
Stir in cooked chickpeas before adding eggs for a heartier meal.
storage: Best served immediately. Refrigerate leftover tomato base up to 3 days; add fresh eggs when reheating.

title: Fluffy Buttermilk Pancakes
summary: Tall, tender buttermilk pancakes with lightly crisp edges, perfect with maple syrup and fresh fruit.
ingredients: Butter or neutral oil for frying
Maple syrup and berries, to serve

stages.title: Mix the dry ingredients
steps: Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and salt together in a large bowl.
Break up any lumps so the raising agents distribute evenly.

stages.title: Mix the wet ingredients
steps: In a jug, whisk eggs, buttermilk, melted cooled butter and vanilla.
Make a well in the dry ingredients and pour in the wet mixture.

stages.title: Combine gently
steps: Fold with a spatula just until no large pockets of dry flour remain. Small lumps are fine.
Let batter rest for 5 minutes while heating the pan; overmixing makes pancakes tough.

stages.title: Cook in batches
steps: Heat a non-stick pan over medium-low heat and lightly grease. Spoon in about 60 ml batter per pancake.
Cook 2–3 minutes until bubbles form and edges look set; flip once and cook another 1–2 minutes until golden and cooked through.

stages.title: Serve warm
steps: Keep cooked pancakes warm on a rack in a low oven while finishing the batch.
Serve with maple syrup, berries or yoghurt.

tips: Use medium-low heat so the centres cook before the outsides brown.
Avoid pressing down after flipping; it deflates the pancakes.
variations: Fold 100 g blueberries into the batter.
Add 1 tsp cinnamon to the dry mix for a warming flavour.
storage: Refrigerate cooked pancakes up to 3 days or freeze with baking paper between them up to 2 months. Reheat in toaster or pan.

title: Greek Salad
summary: Crisp cucumber, juicy tomatoes, olives and feta tossed with oregano and a bright olive oil dressing.
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Cut tomatoes into generous wedges and slice cucumber into thick half-moons.
Thinly slice red onion and capsicum; soak onion in cold water for 5 minutes if you prefer a milder bite, then drain.

stages.title: Make the dressing
steps: Whisk olive oil, red wine vinegar, oregano and a pinch of pepper.
Taste and add a little salt only if needed; feta and olives already provide plenty.

stages.title: Assemble and serve
steps: Arrange vegetables and olives in a broad serving bowl and gently toss with dressing.
Place feta in large pieces on top, scatter a little extra oregano and serve immediately.

tips: Use ripe room-temperature tomatoes for the best flavour.
Keep feta in larger pieces rather than crumbling it finely.
variations: Add a handful of capers for extra brininess.
Serve with warm pita and grilled chicken to make a fuller meal.
storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate undressed chopped vegetables up to 2 days; add feta and dressing just before serving.

title: Garlic Butter Roast Potatoes
summary: Golden roast potatoes with fluffy centres, crisp edges, garlic, butter and fragrant herbs.
ingredients: 1 kg floury potatoes (such as Maris Piper or Sebago)

stages.title: Parboil the potatoes
steps: Heat oven to 220°C conventional (200°C fan). Peel potatoes if desired and cut into even 4–5 cm pieces.
Boil in well-salted water for 8–10 minutes until the edges are just beginning to soften, then drain thoroughly.

stages.title: Rough up the edges
steps: Return drained potatoes to the empty hot pot and shake gently to fluff up their surfaces.
Leave uncovered for 3–5 minutes so steam escapes; dry surfaces roast more crisply.

stages.title: Roast until golden
steps: Heat olive oil in a large roasting tray in the oven for 5 minutes. Carefully add potatoes in a single layer and turn to coat.
Roast 35–40 minutes, turning halfway, until deeply golden and crisp. Avoid crowding the tray.

stages.title: Add garlic butter
steps: Melt butter with crushed garlic and rosemary in a small pan over low heat for 2 minutes without browning garlic.
Toss potatoes with fragrant butter and roast a further 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper before serving.

tips: Floury potatoes give the fluffiest centres.
Do not add garlic at the start of roasting; it can burn at high heat.
variations: Use thyme instead of rosemary.
Add a little finely grated lemon zest after roasting.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat uncovered in a hot oven or air fryer until crisp and steaming hot.

title: Classic Chocolate Brownies
summary: Fudgy chocolate brownies with a crackly top, deep cocoa flavour and a soft, rich centre.

stages.title: Prepare the tin
steps: Heat oven to 175°C conventional (155°C fan). Line a 20 cm square tin with baking paper, leaving overhang.
Measure ingredients before starting so the chocolate mixture does not cool too far.

stages.title: Melt chocolate and butter
steps: Melt butter and chocolate together over very low heat or in short microwave bursts, stirring until smooth.
Set aside for a few minutes so it is warm rather than hot before mixing with eggs.

stages.title: Mix the batter
steps: Whisk eggs and sugar for 2–3 minutes until slightly thickened; stir in vanilla.
Fold in melted chocolate mixture, then sift in flour, cocoa and salt. Mix only until no dry streaks remain.

stages.title: Bake until just set
steps: Spread batter evenly in the tin and bake 24–30 minutes.
The edges should be set and the centre should have a slight wobble; a skewer should show moist crumbs rather than wet batter.

stages.title: Cool before slicing
steps: Cool completely in the tin so the centre firms up.
Lift out using the baking paper and cut into nine squares with a sharp knife.

tips: Do not overbake; brownies continue setting as they cool.
For neat slices, chill for 30 minutes and wipe the knife between cuts.
variations: Fold in 80 g toasted walnuts.
Add 1 tsp instant espresso powder to intensify the chocolate flavour.
storage: Keep airtight at room temperature up to 3 days or refrigerate up to 5 days. Freeze squares up to 2 months.

title: Lemon Drizzle Cake
summary: Soft lemon sponge soaked with tangy citrus syrup and finished with a delicate sugary crust.

stages.title: Prepare oven and tin
steps: Heat oven to 180°C conventional (160°C fan). Grease and line a 900 g loaf tin.
Finely zest both lemons, avoiding the bitter white pith.

stages.title: Cream butter and sugar
steps: Beat softened butter and caster sugar for 3–4 minutes until pale and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating after each; add a spoonful of flour if mixture begins to curdle.

stages.title: Finish the batter
steps: Fold in self-raising flour and lemon zest gently, then add milk until batter drops slowly from a spoon.
Spoon into the prepared tin and level the surface.

stages.title: Bake the loaf
steps: Bake 40–50 minutes until golden, springy and a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean.
If browning too quickly, loosely cover with foil during the final 10 minutes.

stages.title: Add the drizzle
steps: Mix juice from the lemons with granulated sugar until combined but still slightly grainy.
Prick the warm cake all over with a skewer, spoon over drizzle and cool in the tin before slicing.

tips: Drizzle while cake is warm so syrup soaks in.
Room-temperature butter and eggs make a smoother batter.
variations: Add 1 tbsp poppy seeds to the batter.
Replace one lemon with an orange for a sweeter citrus note.
storage: Store airtight at room temperature up to 3 days or freeze slices up to 2 months.

title: Chicken Caesar Salad
summary: Crunchy romaine, juicy chicken, Parmesan and croutons tossed in a creamy, punchy Caesar dressing.

stages.title: Make the croutons
steps: Heat oven to 200°C conventional (180°C fan). Toss bread cubes with 2 tbsp olive oil, salt and pepper.
Bake 8–10 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden. Set aside to cool.

stages.title: Cook the chicken
steps: Season chicken with salt and pepper and rub with 1 tbsp olive oil.
Sear in a frying pan over medium heat for 5–6 minutes per side, adjusting for thickness, until the centre reaches 75°C. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.

stages.title: Whisk the dressing
steps: Mash anchovies with garlic and mustard. Whisk in pasteurised yolk or mayonnaise and lemon juice.
Slowly whisk in 60 ml olive oil until creamy; add a spoonful of water if too thick and season to taste.

stages.title: Assemble
steps: Wash and dry romaine leaves thoroughly, then tear into large bite-sized pieces.
Toss lettuce lightly with dressing, add chicken and croutons, and finish with Parmesan shavings.

tips: Dry lettuce thoroughly so the dressing clings rather than becoming watery.
Rest chicken before slicing to keep it juicy.
variations: Use grilled prawns instead of chicken, cooking until opaque throughout.
Add halved boiled eggs for a more filling lunch.
storage: Keep cooked chicken refrigerated up to 3 days. Store lettuce, croutons and dressing separately; assemble just before eating.

title: Mushroom Risotto
summary: Creamy Arborio rice slowly cooked with savoury mushrooms, white wine, stock and Parmesan.

stages.title: Brown the mushrooms
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms in batches to avoid crowding.
Cook until moisture evaporates and edges turn golden; season lightly and set aside.

stages.title: Soften aromatics and toast rice
steps: In a heavy saucepan, warm remaining oil and half the butter. Cook onion gently for 4 minutes until soft, then garlic for 30 seconds.
Add rice and stir for 2 minutes until grains are glossy and lightly translucent around the edges.

stages.title: Reduce wine and add stock
steps: Pour in wine and stir until nearly absorbed. Add a ladle of warm stock and stir regularly until absorbed.
Continue adding stock a ladle at a time for about 18–22 minutes, keeping a gentle simmer, until rice is tender with a slight bite.

stages.title: Finish the risotto
steps: Fold browned mushrooms into the rice and add a little more stock if it looks stiff; risotto should flow slowly across the plate.
Turn off heat and stir in remaining butter, Parmesan and parsley. Cover for 2 minutes, taste and serve immediately.

tips: Keep stock warm to maintain a steady simmer.
Do not rinse risotto rice; its starch creates the creamy texture.
variations: Add a handful of peas during the final 3 minutes.
Use thyme instead of parsley for a woodsy finish.
storage: Best served immediately. Refrigerate leftovers promptly up to 2 days and reheat thoroughly; alternatively form chilled leftovers into arancini.
